name: The church in Pergamos
charge: Holding among them the doctrine of Balaam and the doctrine of the Nicolaitans
summary: Christ granted that the congregation at Pergamos, dwelling where Satan’s seat is, held fast his name and had not denied his faith even when Antipas was slain among them, and then charged them with having there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balak to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, and them that hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitans (Revelation 2:13-15). The sentence is repentance or the sword of his mouth, and the promise to the one who repents is hidden manna and a white stone with a new name (Revelation 2:16-17).
offenseFull: The doctrine of Balaam is not a mystery; the history is in Numbers. Balaam could not curse Israel and knew it, so he gave counsel instead, and the counsel was women. The daughters of Moab called the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down and joined themselves to Baalpeor, and a plague ran through the congregation (Numbers 25:1-3), and Moses afterwards said these were the very women who caused the children of Israel through the counsel of Balaam to commit trespass in the matter of Peor (Numbers 31:15-16). Our enemies have always known this is the weakness. Holofernes was told plainly that if there is sin in this people it will be their ruin, and if there is no iniquity in the nation then pass them by, lest their Lord defend them (Judith 5:20-21). Keep the people in sin and you can overtake them, because the connection with God is severed. Peter describes the man himself: forsaking the right way, gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness (2 Peter 2:15). There were men in the body who wanted nothing but money.

The second thing was them that hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitans, which Christ says outright that he hates (Revelation 2:15). Nicolas was a proselyte of Antioch, one of the seven chosen out to serve when the widows were being neglected (Acts 6:5), a man converted first to the sacrifices and then to Christ and then set over an office. The accounts read in class say the sect that carried his name lived in unrestrained indulgence and held it a matter of indifference what a man ate and how he lived, shameless in uncleanness, which is the same fornication and the same idolatry named in the verse before it, and the same seduction of Israel into immoral and idolatrous unions with the women of Moab. It is also the exact opposite of what the apostles had settled: abstain from pollutions of idols, from fornication, from things strangled, and from blood (Acts 15:28-29). God hates it because it is the worship of other gods, and his name is Jealous (Exodus 34:14). Ephesus is commended in the same chapter for hating those deeds (Revelation 2:6).
judgmentFull: Repent, or else he comes quickly and will fight against them with the sword of his mouth (Revelation 2:16). That sword is the sharp sword that goes out of his mouth to smite the nations and rule them with a rod of iron (Revelation 19:15); with righteousness he judges the poor, and with the breath of his lips he slays the wicked (Isaiah 11:4), and the wicked whom he consumes with the spirit of his mouth and destroys with the brightness of his coming (2 Thessalonians 2:8). The warning is for our own nation as much as for the heathen: follow what the other nations do and you get what the other nations get. There is no exemption for unrepentant Israel.

On the other side of the repentance is the promise: hidden manna, a white stone, and in the stone a new name written which no man knows except the one who receives it (Revelation 2:17). The manna is Christ. Their fathers ate manna in the wilderness and are dead; he is the bread of life which comes down from heaven, that a man may eat of it and not die (John 6:31-35,48-51). It is hidden because the gospel is hid to them that are lost (2 Corinthians 4:3), which is why the world still cannot say who the black Messiah is or who he came for, and why undoing what was taught about it is the work. The verdict here is reprieve, not sentence. Christ set down what was right with them before he named what was wrong, and the sword only comes out if they will not turn.

lawsResolved.text: Duty and Purpose of the Church (section)

text.text: And to the angel of the church in Pergamos write; These things saith he which hath the sharp sword with two edges;

I know thy works, and where thou dwellest, even where Satan’s seat is: and thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth.

But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication.
And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.
And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.
And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.
And Moses said unto them, Have ye saved all the women alive?
Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.

Now therefore, my lord and governor, if there be any error against this people, and they sin against their God, let us consider that this shall be their ruin, and let us go up, and we shall overcome them.
But if there be no iniquity in their nation, let my lord now pass by, lest their Lord defend them, and their God be for them, and we become a reproach before all the world.
Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness;
So hast thou also them that hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitans, which thing I hate.

And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch:
For it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us, to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things;
That ye abstain from meats offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication: from which if ye keep yourselves, ye shall do well. Fare ye well.
For thou shalt worship no other god: for the Lord, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God:
But this thou hast, that thou hatest the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
Repent; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will fight against them with the sword of my mouth.

And out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron: and he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God.

But with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.
And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming:

He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.
Our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.
Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.
Then said they unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread.
And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.
I am that bread of life.
Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness, and are dead.
This is the bread which cometh down from heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die.
I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.
But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost:
